questions.question: A dining - set listed at Rs. 5000 is sold to a man at successive discounts of 20% and 10% by the shopkeeper. What is the selling price of the dining set?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The marked price = Rs. 5000

The discount successive = 20% and 10% respectively

**Concept:**

Discount = Marked price - Selling price

**Formula used:**

{D\%}={MP-SPover MP} times 100 Where, D = Discount, MP = Marked price, and SP = Selling price

**Calculation:**

Let the final selling price after two successive discounts be X.

According to the question

The selling price after 20% discount = ({1-{20over100}})times 5000= {4over5}times 5000 = 4000

The selling price after 10% discount = {(1-{10over100})}times 4000= {9over10}times 4000 = Rs. 3600

**∴ The required result will be Rs. 3600.**

questions.question: 40 percent of the cost price of an article is equal to the 25 percent of its selling price. What is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equating the given percentages directly gives the ratio of Cost Price to Selling Price:

40% of CP = 25% of SP

CP / SP = 25 / 40 = 5 / 8

Let CP = 5 units and SP = 8 units, which means Profit = 8 − 5 = 3 units.

Profit % = (3 / 5) × 100 = 60%

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

40% of Cost Price (CP) = 25% of Selling Price (SP)

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/287e3706f3c0efd42a01ad110f67d3700c3f507a5617f907c75063aecd577bd3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (40 / 100) × CP = (25 / 100) × SP

⇒ 40 × CP = 25 × SP

⇒ CP / SP = 25 / 40

⇒ CP / SP = 5 / 8

⇒ Let the Cost Price be 5x and the Selling Price be 8x.

⇒ Profit = SP − CP

⇒ Profit = 8x − 5x = 3x

⇒ Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (3x / 5x) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (3 / 5) × 100 = 60%

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

When Cost Price is greater than Selling Price, a loss is incurred. The loss percentage is calculated as: Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). The selling price becomes: SP = MP − Discount. The discount percentage is given by: Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Successive Discounts

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the effective single equivalent discount can be calculated using the formula: [a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)]%.

questions.question: The compound interest on Rs. 60000 at 4% per annum is Rs. 4896. What is the time period in years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The sum = Rs. 60000

The rate of percentage = 4%

The compound interest = Rs. 4896

**Formula used:**

{CI}= {P × [(1+{Rover100})^T - 1]} Where, SI = Simple interest, CI = Compound interest, P = Principle, R = Rate, and T = Time

**Calculation:**

Let the time be T

⇒ {4896}= {60000 × [(1+{4over100})^T - 1]}

⇒ {4896over60000}+1 = {(1+{4over100})^T }

⇒ {64896over 60000} = {(1+{4over100})^T }

⇒ {10816over 10000} = ({104over100})^T

⇒ ({104over100})²=({104over100})^T

⇒ T = 2 

**∴ The required result will be 2 years.**

questions.question: Pinki and Rinki together can do a piece of work in 20 days. Rinki and Minki together can do it in 12 days while Pinki and Minki together can do it in 15 days. In how long can Rinki alone do it?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(20, 12, 15) = 60 units.

Efficiency: (Pinki+Rinki) = 3, (Rinki+Minki) = 5, (Pinki+Minki) = 4.

2 × (Pinki+Rinki+Minki) efficiency = 3 + 5 + 4 = 12 ⇒ P+R+M = 6 units/day.

Rinki efficiency = (P+R+M) − (Pinki+Minki) = 6 − 4 = 2 units/day.

Time for Rinki = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 day.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by (Pinki + Rinki) = 20 days

Time taken by (Rinki + Minki) = 12 days

Time taken by (Pinki + Minki) = 15 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time Taken

Combined efficiency of 2 × (Pinki + Rinki + Minki) = 3 + 5 + 4 = 12 units/day

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total efficiency of (Pinki + Rinki + Minki) = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of Rinki = Efficiency of (Pinki + Rinki + Minki) − Efficiency of (Pinki + Minki)

⇒ Efficiency of Rinki = 6 − 4 = 2 units/day

⇒ Time taken by Rinki alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of Rinki

⇒ Time taken by Rinki alone = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 days

**∴ The correct answer is 30 day.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken. If a person takes T days to complete work, their efficiency is 1/T units per day.

Combined Work Formula

When pairs are given, the total efficiency 2 × (A+B+C) = Eff(A+B) + Eff(B+C) + Eff(C+A). Individual efficiency is found by subtracting the pair that does not include the target person.

Work and Wages

In any piece of work, wages are always distributed in the ratio of the amount of work done by each individual, which depends on their efficiency and time spent working.

questions.question: A sphere of radius 18 cm is melted and then a solid cylinder of base radius 4 cm is made from it. What is the height of the solid cylinder?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The radius of the sphere = 18 cm

The base radius of the cylinder = 4 cm

**Concept:**

If you are melting of a solid into another solid, then volume will be same

**Formula used:**

Volume of the sphere = {4over 3}× π × r³ Where, r = The radius of the sphere

Volume of the cylinder = π × r² × h Where, r = Base radius of the cylinder, h = Height of the cylinder

**Calculation:**

Let the height of the cylinder be h

According to the question

⇒ {4over 3}× π × 18³ = π × 42 × h 

⇒ {4over 3} × 18× 18× 18 = 4 × 4 × h 

⇒ 4 × 6 × 18 × 18 = 4 × 4 × h

⇒ 6 × 18 × 18 = 4 × h

⇒ 3 × 9 × 18 = h

⇒ h = 486 cm

**∴ The required result will be 486 cm.**

questions.question: The difference between cost price and selling price is Rs. 143. If profit percentage is 26 percent, then what is the selling price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The difference between the Selling Price and Cost Price is the Profit.

Profit = 26% of Cost Price ⇒ 26 units = Rs. 143

Selling Price = 100% (CP) + 26% (Profit) = 126 units

Selling Price = (143 ÷ 26) × 126 = 11 × 63 = 693

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 693.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Difference between Cost Price (CP) and Selling Price (SP) = Profit = Rs. 143

Profit percentage = 26%

 Cost Price (100%) Profit (26%) Rs. 143 
• 
• 
• Selling Price (126%) = Rs. 693 Profit and Loss Visualisation 

**Formula Used:**

Profit = (Profit% ÷ 100) × CP

SP = CP + Profit

**Calculations:**

⇒ 143 = (26 ÷ 100) × CP

⇒ CP = (143 × 100) ÷ 26

⇒ CP = 11 × 50

⇒ CP = Rs. 550

⇒ SP = CP + Profit

⇒ SP = 550 + 143

⇒ SP = Rs. 693

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 693.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when the Selling Price (SP) is greater than the Cost Price (CP). Thus, Profit = SP − CP. Conversely, a loss happens when CP is greater than SP.

Profit Percentage Base

Profit and loss percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless the question specifically mentions calculating it on the Selling Price. Formula: Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Direct Selling Price Formula

When the cost price and profit percentage are known, the selling price can be directly calculated using the multiplier formula: SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

questions.question: A sum of money at simple interest amounts to Rs. 800 in 3 years and to Rs. 900 in 4 years. The sum is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The sum of money at simple interest amounts = Rs. 800 in 3 years

The sum of money at simple interest amounts = Rs. 900 in 4 years

**Formula used:**

S.I.={P × R × Tover 100} Where, S.I. = Simple interest, P = Principle, R = Rate, and T = Time

**Calculation:**

Let the sum is P

The simple interest for one year = 900 - 800 = 100

The simple interest for 3 years = 3 × 100 = 300

The amount = The sum + Simple interest

⇒ 800 = P + 300

⇒ P = 500

**∴ The required result will be Rs. 500.**
